{
  "hexsha": "0f71f852a96af9685858ce59fda34ecbf85c283d",
  "one_line_summary": "phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()",
  "vulnerability_summary": "pep_get_sb() calls pskb_may_pull() which may relocate skb head data, then dereferences the stale pointer ph obtained before the pull, causing a slab use-after-free read.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Code saves a pointer to skb header data, calls pskb_may_pull() which may reallocate and invalidate that pointer, then dereferences the stale pointer afterward.",
  "patch": "commit 0f71f852a96af9685858ce59fda34ecbf85c283d
Author: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
Date:   Tue Jul 21 01:58:45 2026 -0700

    phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()
    
    pep_get_sb() doesn't consider that pskb_may_pull() might have relocated
    the skb data, and continue to access the older pointer, causing UAF.
    
    Reproduced under KASAN:
    
      BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0
      Read of size 1 at addr ff11000105510f50 by task repro/157
       pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0
       pipe_handler_do_rcv+0x5f7/0xa10
       pep_do_rcv+0x203/0x410
       __sk_receive_skb+0x471/0x4a0
       phonet_rcv+0x5b3/0x6c0
       __netif_receive_skb+0xcc/0x1d0
    
    Refetch the header with skb_header_pointer() after pskb_may_pull(), so
    the possibly stale pointer is no longer dereferenced. There are better
    ways to solve this, but, this is the less instrusive one.
    
    Fixes: 9641458d3ec4 ("Phonet: Pipe End Point for Phonet Pipes protocol")
    Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
    Signed-off-by: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260721-phonet_get_sb_uaf-v1-1-95fd7881cc4e@debian.org
    Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/phonet/pep.c b/net/phonet/pep.c
index 706927139393..31b29e3ca7bc 100644
--- a/net/phonet/pep.c
+++ b/net/phonet/pep.c
@@ -55,6 +55,8 @@ static unsigned char *pep_get_sb(struct sk_buff *skb, u8 *ptype, u8 *plen,
 	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	if (ph == NULL || ph->sb_len < 2 || !pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len))
 		return NULL;
+	/* pskb_may_pull() may have reallocated the head; refetch ph. */
+	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	ph->sb_len -= 2;
 	*ptype = ph->sb_type;
 	*plen = ph->sb_len;
"
}

  "one_line_summary": "phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()",
  "vulnerability_summary": "pep_get_sb() calls pskb_may_pull() which may relocate skb head data, then dereferences the stale pointer ph obtained before the pull, causing a slab use-after-free read.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Code saves a pointer to skb header data, calls pskb_may_pull() which may reallocate and invalidate that pointer, then dereferences the stale pointer afterward.",
  "patch": "commit 0f71f852a96af9685858ce59fda34ecbf85c283d
Author: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
Date:   Tue Jul 21 01:58:45 2026 -0700

    phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()
    
    pep_get_sb() doesn't consider that pskb_may_pull() might have relocated
    the skb data, and continue to access the older pointer, causing UAF.
    
    Reproduced under KASAN:
    
      BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0
      Read of size 1 at addr ff11000105510f50 by task repro/157

       pipe_handler_do_rcv+0x5f7/0xa10
       pep_do_rcv+0x203/0x410
       __sk_receive_skb+0x471/0x4a0
       phonet_rcv+0x5b3/0x6c0
       __netif_receive_skb+0xcc/0x1d0
    
    Refetch the header with skb_header_pointer() after pskb_may_pull(), so
    the possibly stale pointer is no longer dereferenced. There are better
    ways to solve this, but, this is the less instrusive one.
    
    Fixes: 9641458d3ec4 ("Phonet: Pipe End Point for Phonet Pipes protocol")
    Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
    Signed-off-by: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260721-phonet_get_sb_uaf-v1-1-95fd7881cc4e@debian.org
    Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/phonet/pep.c b/net/phonet/pep.c
index 706927139393..31b29e3ca7bc 100644
--- a/net/phonet/pep.c
+++ b/net/phonet/pep.c
@@ -55,6 +55,8 @@ static unsigned char *pep_get_sb(struct sk_buff *skb, u8 *ptype, u8 *plen,
 	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	if (ph == NULL || ph->sb_len < 2 || !pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len))
 		return NULL;
+	/* pskb_may_pull() may have reallocated the head; refetch ph. */
+	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	ph->sb_len -= 2;
 	*ptype = ph->sb_type;
 	*plen = ph->sb_len;
"
}

{
  "hexsha": "0f71f852a96af9685858ce59fda34ecbf85c283d",
  "one_line_summary": "phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()",
  "vulnerability_summary": "pep_get_sb() calls pskb_may_pull() which may relocate skb head data, then dereferences the stale pointer ph obtained before the pull, causing a slab use-after-free read.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Code saves a pointer to skb header data, calls pskb_may_pull() which may reallocate and invalidate that pointer, then dereferences the stale pointer afterward.",
  "patch": "commit 0f71f852a96af9685858ce59fda34ecbf85c283d
Author: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
Date:   Tue Jul 21 01:58:45 2026 -0700

    phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()
    
    pep_get_sb() doesn't consider that pskb_may_pull() might have relocated
    the skb data, and continue to access the older pointer, causing UAF.
    
    Reproduced under KASAN:
    
      BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0
      Read of size 1 at addr ff11000105510f50 by task repro/157
       pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0
       pipe_handler_do_rcv+0x5f7/0xa10
       pep_do_rcv+0x203/0x410
       __sk_receive_skb+0x471/0x4a0
       phonet_rcv+0x5b3/0x6c0
       __netif_receive_skb+0xcc/0x1d0
    
    Refetch the header with skb_header_pointer() after pskb_may_pull(), so
    the possibly stale pointer is no longer dereferenced. There are better
    ways to solve this, but, this is the less instrusive one.
    
    Fixes: 9641458d3ec4 ("Phonet: Pipe End Point for Phonet Pipes protocol")
    Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
    Signed-off-by: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260721-phonet_get_sb_uaf-v1-1-95fd7881cc4e@debian.org
    Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/phonet/pep.c b/net/phonet/pep.c
index 706927139393..31b29e3ca7bc 100644
--- a/net/phonet/pep.c
+++ b/net/phonet/pep.c
@@ -55,6 +55,8 @@ static unsigned char *pep_get_sb(struct sk_buff *skb, u8 *ptype, u8 *plen,
 	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	if (ph == NULL || ph->sb_len < 2 || !pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len))
 		return NULL;
+	/* pskb_may_pull() may have reallocated the head; refetch ph. */
+	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	ph->sb_len -= 2;
 	*ptype = ph->sb_type;
 	*plen = ph->sb_len;
"
}

Author: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
Date:   Tue Jul 21 01:58:45 2026 -0700

    phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()
    
    pep_get_sb() doesn't consider that pskb_may_pull() might have relocated
    the skb data, and continue to access the older pointer, causing UAF.
    
    Reproduced under KASAN:
    
      BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0

       __sk_receive_skb+0x471/0x4a0
       phonet_rcv+0x5b3/0x6c0
       __netif_receive_skb+0xcc/0x1d0
    
    Refetch the header with skb_header_pointer() after pskb_may_pull(), so
    the possibly stale pointer is no longer dereferenced. There are better
    ways to solve this, but, this is the less instrusive one.
    
    Fixes: 9641458d3ec4 ("Phonet: Pipe End Point for Phonet Pipes protocol")
    Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
    Signed-off-by: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>

    Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/phonet/pep.c b/net/phonet/pep.c
index 706927139393..31b29e3ca7bc 100644
--- a/net/phonet/pep.c
+++ b/net/phonet/pep.c
@@ -55,6 +55,8 @@ static unsigned char *pep_get_sb(struct sk_buff *skb, u8 *ptype, u8 *plen,
 	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	if (ph == NULL || ph->sb_len < 2 || !pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len))
 		return NULL;
+	/* pskb_may_pull() may have reallocated the head; refetch ph. */
+	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	ph->sb_len -= 2;
 	*ptype = ph->sb_type;
 	*plen = ph->sb_len;
"
}

import re, os, sys, json

PULL_RE = re.compile(r'\b(pskb_may_pull|pskb_pull|pskb_pull_reserve|__pskb_pull_tail|skb_linearize)\s*\(')
CAP_TYPES = r'(?:const\s+)?(?:struct\s+\w+|unsigned\s+char|u8|u16|u32|__be16|__be32|__wsum|void|char)'
CAPTURE_RE = re.compile(r'^(?P<indent>\s*)' + CAP_TYPES + r'\s*\**\s*(?P<var>\w+)\s*=\s*(?P<rhs>[^;]+);$')
RHS_HINT = re.compile(r'skb->data|skb_header_pointer|\w+_hdr\(skb|mpls_hdr\(|skb_network_header|skb_transport_header|skb_mac_header|skb->head|skb_tail_pointer')

def find_func_bounds(lines, idx):
    start = idx
    while start > 0:
        s = lines[start]
        if s.startswith('{') or (s.rstrip().endswith('{') and not s[0].isspace()):
            break
        start -= 1
    depth = 0
    end = start
    i = start
    while i < len(lines):
        depth += lines[i].count('{') - lines[i].count('}')
        if i > start and depth <= 0:
            end = i
            break
        if i == start and depth <= 0 and '{' in lines[start]:
            end = i
            break
        i += 1
    return start, min(end, len(lines)-1)

def scan_file(path):
    results = []
    with open(path, 'r', errors='replace') as f:
        lines = f.readlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if not PULL_RE.search(line):
            continue
        try:
            fs, fe = find_func_bounds(lines, i)
        except Exception:
            continue
        if fs >= fe:
            continue
        captures = []
        for j in range(fs, i+1):
            cm = CAPTURE_RE.match(lines[j])
            if cm:
                var = cm.group('var')
                rhs = cm.group('rhs')
                if RHS_HINT.search(rhs):
                    captures.append((j, var, rhs.strip()))
        if not captures:
            continue
        for (cj, var, rhs) in captures:
            # find first post-pull use and refetch
            first_use = None
            refetch_before_use = False
            refetch_line = None
            for j in range(i+1, fe+1):
                l = lines[j]
                if re.match(r'^\s*' + re.escape(var) + r'\s*=[^=]', l):
                    refetch_before_use = True
                    refetch_line = j+1
                    break
                if re.search(r'\b' + re.escape(var) + r'\b', l):
                    first_use = (j+1, l.strip()[:130])
                    break
            if first_use:
                results.append({
                    'file': path,
                    'capture_line': cj+1,
                    'capture': ('%s = %s' % (var, rhs))[:140],
                    'pull_line': i+1,
                    'pull': line.strip()[:130],
                    'refetched': refetch_before_use,
                    'refetch_line': refetch_line,
                    'first_use': first_use,
                })
    return results

base = os.getcwd()
allres = []
with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
    for rel in f.read().split():
        path = rel if rel.startswith('/') else os.path.join(base, rel)
        if not os.path.exists(path):
